chunks: Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū Maryam al-Anṣārī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man fasted some part of the month of Ramaḍān and then remained ill until he died, then there is no qaḍāʾ upon him. But if he recovered, then fell ill, then died, and he had wealth, charity should be given on his behalf in place of each day, a mudd for every day. And if he did not have wealth, his guardian should fast on his behalf.

key_terms.تُصُدِّقَ: charity is to be given on someone's behalf
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the obligatory period of fasting
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: make-up performance of missed obligatory fasts
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth from which compensation may be given
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: ill; in a state of sickness affecting legal duty
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a mudd, a fixed measure of food used for expiatory charity
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his guardian or legal heir responsible to act on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on missed Ramaḍān fasts if someone dies after illness?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for missed Ramaḍān fasts when a person dies after illness. If continuous illness prevented recovery until death, no make-up fasts are due; but if the person recovered and later died, compensation is made either by charity from his wealth or by fasting from his guardian if he had no wealth.
